Subject: SLA gatekeeper: load & latency targets / proposed test window

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the runbook template. Before we lock in schedules, Orbit needs to validate the following acceptance criteria during onboarding so Procurement can finalize the dev-to-prod uplift: 

- p95 inference latency <= 250 ms for 512-token requests
- sustained throughput of 300–350 req/s for our steady-state traffic pattern (mix: 60% short prompts, 40% long)
- <0.5% error rate across 10M token window

We'd like a short smoke + soak during the week of May 8 and a heavier load validation on May 9 (Pacific window: 02:00–06:00 PDT) if that works for your infra team. Attached is our sample load profile (orbit_load_profile_v1.csv) and a high-level ramp plan.

Can you confirm the run owner and any configuration we should apply on our side (client concurrency, batching hints, auth/test keys)? Also, please confirm whether KV cache will be warmed for the ramp.

Cheers,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Integrations | Orbit Payments

Attachments: orbit_load_profile_v1.csv (csv), ramp-plan-20280502.pdf (pdf)

On Tue, May 2, 2028 at 10:03 AM monica_patel@redwood.ai wrote:
> Ben / Rishi / Laura — forwarding Orbit's acceptance targets and proposed windows...

Plan and quick notes from infra:
- Test harness: we'll use our in-house runner (redwood-load) which surfaces per-request latency and token-level cost. It can replay CSV profiles (use the attached orbit_load_profile_v1.csv).
- KV cache: recommend warming with representative prefixes for 30 minutes before the soak; we'll run a separate warmup traffic set at 20% of target. Mark test as KV-warm vs cold in results.
- Quantization/profile: run in q4_8 mode for throughput-first tests; run one short pass in q6_8 to validate tail latency differences.
- Metrics to collect: p50/p75/p95/p99 latency, errors (500/429), CPU/GPU utilization, GPU memory, HBM stalls, token-per-second, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Infrastructure note: please allocate a dedicated pool for Orbit during the run (no multi-tenant burst) to avoid noisy neighbors.

I'll own the run and the final results artifact. Ben — can you own the external coordination and confirm the exact start time with Samantha? Laura — please prepare the post-test acceptance checklist template (I put a stub in the Drive link).

-rishi
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the details. Confirming Redwood will own the run on May 9 (02:00–05:30 PDT) with the following flow:

1) 02:00–02:20 — smoke and auth check (10% traffic)
2) 02:20–03:20 — 1h soak at 50% target (150 req/s) with KV warmup preceding at 30 minutes
3) 03:20–03:50 — cooldown and reconfig to q4_8 -> then 04:00–05:30 — 90m sustained spike to 325–350 req/s (collect full telemetry)

Deliverables: full metrics CSV, p50/p95/p99 breakdown, error log, GPU telemetry, annotated run flags (redwood-run-annotations.txt), and a short acceptance memo stating pass/fail on each SLA gate. We'll upload artifacts to the Drive link and drop a JIRA comment on ONB-452 when results are available.

Can you confirm:
- test keys (we'll use the sandbox key you already provided: orbit-sbx-2028)
- whether you want the run to include a small subset of real user prompts (you can redact) vs synthetic prompts — we recommend a 70/30 real/synthetic mix for signal.

If that's all good I'll lock the slot and run.

Best,
Monica
